name: Corey Gates
headline: CTO and VP Engineering at Caspar.ai
about: Engineering veteran with 20+ years of experience managing hardware and software product life cycles from inception to general availability. Key involvement in five successful start-up companies holding executive and engineering management positions. Interests include information and communication technology, software development processes and methodologies, and human-machine interfaces.

experiences.description: Oversee engineering and product development. Caspar is a rapidly growing, global company headquartered in Silicon Valley with offices in Las Vegas, Rotterdam and Tokyo. Caspar enables retirement communities to provide better and more efficient care for seniors and families through unique AI and next-generation features.

Oversaw technology across all business units at Icontrol Networks, a widely distributed connected home platform. Managed multiple engineering teams developing end-to-end software and hardware, including mobile applications, cloud services, customer premise middleware and firmware.

Performed consulting work in telecommunications and voice over IP technology for key clients including Nextel Communications and Sprint. Provided clients with expert advice in packet communication technologies, critical vendor evaluations and strategic direction related to industry standards and new communication technologies.  Developed commercial grade push-to-talk system  that leveraged a custom interface to interwork with the Nextel dispatch system.

Joined the HearMe executive management team to lead technology products in engineering department, which consisted of 60 people including development, operations and quality assurance.  Managed development and release of the HearMe VoiceSERVER, VoiceCLIENT and SoftPHONE products, including overseeing budget, schedules and objectives. Invited to speak at industry conferences to discuss HearMe technologies. Involved in industry standards organizations to promote company and its technologies.

Co-founded AudioTalk, a voice over IP conferencing bridge company. Grew company to 40 people, recruiting 25 developers and managers into the engineering department. HearMe acquired AudioTalk in early 2000 for $125 million in cash and stock. Played a key role in technology development and system architecture, including design of specialized hardware with 16 DSPs and 100 Mbps Ethernet packet interface. Participated in development of the H.323 and SIP stacks, as well as the AudioTalk MCU software architecture.

Responsible for development of H.323/H.321 gateway (V-Gate 5000), including writing the H.323 stack and embedded DSP software as well as participating in its hardware design. Successfully brought the product through complete lifecycle to general availability. Provided leadership to the gateway team, overseeing system architecture and monitoring development goals.
Responsible for audio portion of PC3000/PC300 product line. Designed and shipped the audio hardware card that included 56000 DSP, audio interface and modern interface.
